input: Design and print custom bookplates for my library

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing how many bookplates are needed and whether one design covers all books or multiple variants are required determines the scale of the design and print job.
The bookplates could be for a single person, a family, a club, or a gifted set — this changes the name, crest, and tone used in the design.
Bookplate aesthetics range from classic heraldic engravings to minimal modern type — the visual style completely drives the design direction.
Budget determines whether professional printing, home printing, or a print-on-demand service is used, and how premium the materials can be.
Whether the user will design the bookplates themselves, hire a designer, or use a template tool is the most immediate fork in the action path.
The physical size and label format needed depends on the books themselves — large art books vs. pocket paperbacks call for different dimensions and adhesive types.
The user may prioritise a heirloom-quality keepsake feel, quick functional labelling, or a giftable product — this sets the quality bar for the whole project.

gold.taskTitle: Design and print custom bookplates for my library
gold.taskDescription: Create personalised bookplates — decorative labels bearing the owner's name or mark — to be printed and placed inside books in a personal library.

questions.title: How many bookplates do you need to print?
questions.description: Establish the total quantity required — e.g. 20 for a small shelf vs. 200+ for a large collection — to guide format and print method choices.

questions.title: Whose name or identity should the bookplate show?
questions.description: Clarify whether the bookplates represent an individual, a family name, a couple, or an institution, as this shapes the text and any crest or monogram.

questions.title: What visual style are you drawn to for the design?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a classic/heraldic look, a vintage woodcut style, clean modern typography, illustrative, or something else entirely.

questions.title: What is your budget for this project?
questions.description: Understand the financial envelope — from zero-cost home printing on sticker paper to professional letterpress or foil printing — to recommend the right production route.

questions.title: Will you design them yourself or hire someone?
questions.description: Identify whether the user wants a DIY template tool, plans to use design software themselves, or wants to commission a designer or print service.

questions.title: What size and label format do your books need?
questions.description: Determine the target dimensions and backing type — e.g. a standard 3x4 inch self-adhesive label vs. a gummed or loose sheet — based on the books' inside covers.

questions.title: What does a successful bookplate feel like to you?
questions.description: Uncover the quality bar and end goal — a cherished heirloom item, a practical ownership label, a gift for someone, or a decorative collector's piece.
